title: Secretary of State of Nevada

context.text: The race is a rematch: in 2022 Aguilar defeated Marchant 48.9% to 46.7%. Aguilar was unopposed in the Democratic primary; Marchant won a four-way Republican primary on June 9 with 32.6%, ahead of Shirley Folkins-Roberts (30.6%), Sharron Angle (26.2%) and Socorro Keenan (3.4%).
Voters will also decide Question 7, a constitutional amendment requiring voter ID that voters first approved in 2024 with about 73%.

Clark County's official Nov. 3, 2026 contest and candidate list (Aug. 24, 2026) shows four candidates for Secretary of State: Francisco "Cisco" Aguilar (Democratic), Brad Lee Barnhill (Independent American), John T. Kennedy (Libertarian) and Jim Marchant (Republican).

candidates.name: Cisco Aguilar
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary (canceled).

priorities.text: Modernizing business licensing and making Nevada more competitive for businesses.
Strengthening election integrity by prioritizing cybersecurity and advocating for election workers.
Promoting civic engagement, including recruiting poll workers with Vet the Vote and boosting turnout among Native American communities and young voters.

record.text: According to his campaign site, he championed a bipartisan bill making it a felony to harass or dox election officials, which passed the Nevada Legislature unanimously.
His campaign site, as quoted by Ballotpedia, says the statewide voter registration system was implemented in record time and the business filing system is easier to use.

priorities.text: Election integrity plan: voter ID, paper ballots counted by hand at the precinct level, ending universal mail-in voting, requiring all voters to re-register, and leaving the Electronic Registration Information Center.
Business reform: repeal the Commerce Tax, lower registration costs and streamline filings.

Told News 4 "We don't have a fair and transparent election yet" and that Nevada should get rid of voting machines; when asked whether his 2016 general election and 2022 primary victories were fraudulent, he said he does not believe the results, and claimed without evidence that 20,000 votes were manufactured for Aguilar in 2022, per News 4.

positions.summary: His election integrity plan calls for proof of United States citizenship to register and vote.
positions.quote: Proof of United States citizenship to register and vote

positions.summary: His campaign site supports finishing the border wall, adding Border Patrol agents and launching mass deportations.
positions.quote: launching mass deportations of those who broke our laws to get here

candidates.name: Brad Barnhill
candidates.currentRole: Paralegal; former Clark County IAP chairman

priorities.text: Implement voter ID, if Nevada voters confirm Question 7, with a bipartisan rollout including free or low-cost ID assistance.
Clean up Nevada's voter rolls; his site says he sued in federal court after the office closed his complaint about 12,465 apparent duplicate Clark County registrations.
Repeal the Commerce Tax and modernize state IT systems.

researchNotes: Slate: confirmed against Clark County's official general-election contest list (the Secretary of State's site blocks automated access), including John T. Kennedy (Libertarian), for whom no Ballotpedia page, website or coverage was found. Aguilar's record rests on his campaign site's description of his office's work, because the Secretary of State's website blocked automated access; Marchant's position on proof of citizenship is from his campaign site. A News 4 report says Marchant was involved in the 2020 'fake elector' plan; KTNV and the Nevada Current report that he attended the December 2020 signing but was not one of the six electors, and that the six electors are the ones charged. No charge against Marchant was found, so none is stated here.
